A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical content, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V4 reports original recursive-training experiments, regression analyses, political-bias measurements, judge validation, and appendix simulations.

after.justification: V6 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports regression explained-variance results in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The iterative chain, fresh base-model selection, LoRA training, and human/synthetic data accumulation procedures are retained. The added pseudocode and expanded clustering explanation document the existing procedure without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five Twitter, Reddit, and Wikipedia datasets, US-senator political-bias task, OpenMEVA-ROC judge validation, and toy-simulation scenarios. The added regression diagnostics reuse existing experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the comparison with Chen et al. (2023). The homogeneous-chain comparisons also retain the same four base models. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: V6 adds R² as a diagnostic metric for the existing regression models in Sections 4.3–4.4. Previously reported data processing, model configurations, training budgets, sampling procedures, and generated-text metrics remain unchanged; the addition does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.4 assesses how much variation the existing regression models explain, supplementing coefficient significance with model-fit diagnostics. The model-count robustness experiment, quality manipulations, toy-model analysis, and additional political-bias analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Appendix B.7 explicitly discloses that regression p-values are uncorrected and explains the authors' rationale for interpreting repeated patterns across conditions. The five-seed statement, significance thresholds, and toy simulation's 50-run statement are unchanged; no additional runs or multiplicity correction are reported.

E6.justification: V6 Tables 3–4 add R² results, including pooled values of 0.293 for semantic diversity and 0.737 for quality, and multi-domain Wikipedia values of 0.241 and 0.363 respectively. Tables 1–2 and the substantive findings in the retained figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: The metric constructions and biased-histogram toy model's assumptions and formulation in Appendix C.3 are retained. The added pseudocode and R² results introduce no new mathematical definitions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract changes properties 'predicting' distribution-shift magnitudes to properties 'associated with' them, with corresponding changes to Section 4.3's framing. This modestly narrows the predictive claim; the central contributions concerning dataset dependence, domain modularity, and political-bias dynamics remain.

C2.justification: V6 specifies additional limits on political representativeness and newly acknowledges that judge validation on stories may not transfer to social-media posts. Appendix C.4 interprets the regressions as explaining only part of the variation, while B.7 adds a defense of interpreting uncorrected tests.

D1.justification: V6 adds iterative-chain pseudocode in Appendix B.6/Figure 8, expands the cluster-construction explanation, and newly mentions manual quality inspection of social-media posts. Hardware, training and sampling hyperparameters, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V6 consolidates v4's two Shumailov references, which share authors and Nature volume/pages, into one entry. This is duplicate-reference cleanup; substantive related-work coverage and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V6 makes local grammatical corrections, removes the keyword line, revises predictive terminology, and expands selected limitations and appendix explanations. It adds subsections B.6, B.7, and C.4 while preserving the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: V6 adds pseudocode Figure 8 and R² Tables 3–4. Figures 2, 5, and 6 receive revised labels, legends, or styling, including percentage rather than count axes in Figure 6. Existing appendix figures are renumbered and reflowed within the retained two-column format.

improvement.justification: Compared with v4, v6 makes regression fit assessable through Tables 3–4 and more clearly qualifies judge validity, political representativeness, and predictive claims. These improve transparency and interpretation. The gains are limited: the empirical foundation is unchanged, and B.7's defense of uncorrected tests does not itself resolve multiplicity concerns.
